I'm checking the "the tool loop" card on the how-it-works page, but its address didn't come back, so I won't guess a path like /how-it-works/the-rules. I'll answer without calling ShowPage and offer the user a few choices instead. The core of the answer is that the engine doesn't special-case the tool call; `FunctionInvokingChatClient` runs the loop, and each requested call passes through the guard checks.

I'm laying out the steps of the loop now: the model's function call goes through the guards, where a call cut off at the output limit is skipped and the model is told to write in chunks, then the tool runs with arguments mapped by name. If the tool throws, the error goes back to the model so it can correct itself, and an oversized result is summarised by a separate tool-less model call. After the tenth round the tools stay on the request with tool use switched off, so the model has to answer in text.

I'm adding a note that every request gets priced in the ledger, plus the point that a round's tool calls run in parallel only when every toolset is read-only (ADR 0026). I'll also point to the runtime view doc, with the building block view for the engine, and keep the choices at the end.

The engine doesn't run tools by itself. `FunctionInvokingChatClient` runs the loop. Each tool call the model asks for goes through `ToolCallGuards.InvokeAsync`, which logs it, runs it, and guards the result. The result then goes back to the model, for up to 10 rounds per message.

For one call, the steps are:

1. The model asks for a tool by name, with its arguments as data. The arguments are never pasted into a shell command.
2. A call cut off by the 16,000-token output limit is not run. The model is told to write large content in chunks.
3. The tool runs. It is a public method on a pack's tool class, which the engine registered for the session.
4. If the tool throws, the exception message goes back to the model, so it can correct itself. The failure is logged.
5. If the result is over 50,000 characters, a separate model call with no tools summarises it. If that fails, the result is cut short.
6. The result is added to the conversation, and the model continues. On the last round, the tools stay on the request with tool use switched off, so the model answers in text.

Every request to the model is priced in the usage ledger, one record per round.
